question: How should the preferences of younger investors shape Edward Jones's offerings?

claims.text: The 2024 Bank of America private bank study (published 2024-06-18) reports that 72% of younger investors (ages 21 to 43) believe it is no longer possible to achieve above-average returns solely with traditional stocks and bonds, versus 28% of investors over 44. Among younger high-net-worth investors, 17% of portfolios are in alternatives (5% for older investors), 93% plan to allocate more to alternatives, and 49% own cryptocurrency with another 38% interested.

The 2026 Bank of America private bank study (published 2026-06-17) reports that 67% of younger investors (Gen Z and Millennials, ages 21 to 45) believe traditional stocks and bonds can no longer deliver above-average returns. They allocate 15% to alternatives and 13% to crypto. 58% of the young wealthy own crypto (up from 49% in 2024), and 88% say they are likely to allocate more to alternatives in the next few years, versus 15% of Boomers and Silents.

The FINRA Foundation investor study (published 2025-12-04) finds that investors under 35 are much more likely to own individual stocks than mutual funds (82% vs. 47%), a gap that narrows with age. It also finds 68% of 18-34s have an options-enabled account and 43% have traded options, versus 27% and 10% of those 55+.

The same FINRA Foundation study (published 2025-12-04) reports that half or more of those under 35 say they invest for social responsibility, entertainment and social-activity reasons. It also says younger investors' enthusiasm for these reasons has declined noticeably relative to 2021.

Peer context, Schwab: on its Q4 2025 call (published 2026-01-21), CEO Rick Wurster said Gen Z investors were nearly a third of new retail client accounts opened in 2025, and nearly 60% were under age 40. On its Q3 2026 call (published 2026-10-15), he said approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials, and described Schwab's retail business as built to win across generations.

Edward Jones's own filing: the 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says the Partnership primarily serves individual investors in the U.S. and Canada. It derives revenue primarily from advisory and account-service fees, fees on assets held by clients, and commissions on mutual fund shares, insurance products and securities transactions. The 10-K lists among its goals to be a 'knowledge-powered advice firm' delivering 'data-powered insights to better serve clients'. Its subsidiaries include Edward Jones Trust Company and Olive Street, which advises the Edward Jones Money Market Fund and the twelve sub-advised Bridge Builder Trust funds.

Trade press (Kitces.com article reprinted 2026-08-18; indicative only) reports that Edward Jones took a minority stake in Quicken, with an explicit intention to integrate Quicken's personal financial management capabilities more directly into Edward Jones to support its value proposition and advisor conversations. The article notes Edward Jones says it is still determining the deployment strategy. It cites Edward Jones as having 20,000 advisors and nearly 10 million clients.

Trade press (published 2026-09-30; indicative only) says Edward Jones advisors serve over 263,000 workplace retirement plans with nearly $107 billion in assets under care and more than 1.3 million plan participants. It also says Edward Jones Ventures took part in Aboon's seed round of $17.5 million.

The evidence above only provides objective context for the strategic question asked. Whether or how Edward Jones should act is a judgment for the strategy team to make, beyond the scope of this evidence engine.

adjacent.text: The Bank of America studies cover wealthy and ultra-high-net-worth younger investors (the 2026 text refers to the 'young wealthy'; the 2024 text to 'younger high-net-worth investors').
adjacent.differs_because: They describe affluent younger investors, not Edward Jones's client base or the general younger-investor population.

adjacent.text: The FINRA Foundation study covers U.S. investors by age band (18-34, 35-54, 55+).
adjacent.differs_because: It is a general investor survey, not Edward Jones client data, and uses different age cut-offs from the Bank of America studies.

gaps.what: Edward Jones's own disclosure of the age mix of its clients or new clients (younger-client share), or of its product plans aimed at younger investors, is not in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones earnings materials, investor presentations or management commentary on client demographics and next-generation clients

gaps.what: Edward Jones's offering of alternatives, crypto or options products to younger investors is not found in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones product and platform disclosures (website, Form CRS, 10-K product descriptions)
